questions.q: How does Microsoft officially describe Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric relative to Azure Data Factory?
options: The next generation of Azure Data Factory
An unrelated product with a similar name
A rebrand of Azure Data Factory with no architectural changes
A discontinued predecessor to Azure Data Factory
questions.explain: Microsoft explicitly positions Fabric Data Factory as the next generation of Azure Data Factory, built on a genuinely different, unified architecture.

questions.q: What sits at the foundation of the Fabric Data Factory stack, underneath connectivity, movement, orchestration, and transformation?
questions.explain: OneLake is the unified storage layer everything in Fabric Data Factory sits on top of, letting different workloads reference the same data without copying it.

questions.q: Why is ELT more natural in Fabric than it typically was in classic Azure Data Factory?
options: Fabric's compute and storage are already unified in OneLake, so transformation can happen where the data already sits
Fabric doesn't actually support ETL at all, only ELT
ELT requires no compute resources in Fabric
There's no real difference between ETL and ELT in Fabric
questions.explain: Because OneLake unifies storage and compute, transforming data where it already lives (ELT) is more natural than shipping it to a separate compute resource first.

questions.q: Which of these carries over largely unchanged from classic Azure Data Factory to Fabric Data Factory?
options: Integration runtimes, which work identically in both
Datasets, which work exactly the same way
Nothing carries over — Fabric requires learning everything from scratch
questions.explain: The expression language is nearly identical between the two, so knowledge from Lesson 22 transfers directly, even though other concepts like datasets and integration runtimes change significantly.

questions.q: Roughly how many connectors does Fabric Data Factory support?
options: Exactly 10, covering only Microsoft's own services
Connectors aren't supported in Fabric Data Factory
questions.explain: Fabric Data Factory connects to more than 170 data sources, spanning on-premises, cloud, and multicloud environments — comparable in breadth to classic ADF.
